gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the sign inconsistency between the homogeneous eigenvector (alpha,v), the required (-1,y) normalization, and the resulting reconstruction. Its explicit corrected formula y=-v/alpha and x=-(1/alpha)Q_kv is the same defect and repair as the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the failed sign normalization in the generalized-eigenvector-to-solution reconstruction, which makes the printed x have the wrong sign and invalidates the residual/backward-error identity.

component_coverage.gold_component: The eigenvector and reconstruction use the wrong sign: division by alpha yields first coordinate +1 rather than the required -1, so y and x must carry an additional minus sign.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly derives y=-v_min/alpha from proportionality to [-1;y], points out the erroneous +1 first coordinate, and supplies the corrected negative reconstruction.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an erroneous extra dqds/Cholesky recurrence at k=1 and the resulting false convergence test. ISSUE-003 instead concerns an inverse-iteration iteration-count simplification and does not identify the k=1 initialization or extra update.

The gold issue is a false chi-square tail estimate used in the probabilistic proof. ISSUE-003 identifies a separate arithmetic simplification that drops additive and log-log terms from an inverse-iteration bound; it neither diagnoses nor repairs the false probabilistic inference.

The gold issue is the distinct gap between testing the ideal subspace optimum and certifying the returned approximate minimizer, including a required safety margin or actual-output check. ISSUE-003 only challenges the numerical iteration-count simplification and does not recognize this output-contract obligation.

The gold issue concerns ambiguous presentation of empirical evidence as a possible theoretical lower bound or obstruction. ISSUE-003 concerns an inverse-iteration numerical bound and contains no diagnosis of evidence-status ambiguity or confusion between conjecture and theorem.
